attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post. He is responding to Roose's mention of IMO scores, but the susceptibility claim is his own.

semantics.note: Faithfully says IMO scores are just another benchmark open to exploitation. Unhedged present-tense claim about susceptibility, not an accusation of cheating.

contract.note: Reading the claim as susceptibility through reused published problems fits his 'know the answers ahead of time' mechanism. It narrows his 'same as any other benchmark' wording, since e1 says fresh IMO problems are immune. The result depends on that reading.

evidence.note: FrontierMath preprint, dated before the post. Documents that benchmark problems in training data inflate scores, and says only fresh IMO/AIME problems are immune, implying published ones are not. The IMO-specific Section 5 passage it cites is not in the excerpt.
Calls public IMO problems easily accessible but found no significant memorization by o1-mini. Per the contract, one null result does not establish immunity.
OpenAI disclosure names AIME, not IMO, which leaves unclear which evaluation was meant. Company disclosure; not evidence on IMO contamination.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's fair plain reading, documented vulnerability is enough. e1 shows that contamination from published benchmark problems inflates scores and that only fresh competition problems escape it, so published IMO problems are susceptible. e2's null result for one model does not show immunity. Limits: the referenced evaluation is unidentified, and nothing shows that particular scores were inflated.
